<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
</rules>

<clingo_essentials>

Every statement ends with `.`. Three forms:
  fact:        pred(a, b).
  rule:        head :- body.
  constraint:  :- body.

Aggregates use `{ }`, not `( )`. Available: `#count`, `#sum`, `#min`, `#max`.
Aggregates go on the right side of `=`:
  val(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.

Choice rules guess values within bounds. Each choice contains exactly ONE atom:
  1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

Modulo is `\`, integer division is `/`. There is no `#mod`, no `//`, no `?:` ternary.

**Safety rule (the most important rule):** every variable in a rule body must
appear in at least one positive (non-negated) predicate. The following do
NOT bind variables:
  - `not` (negation)
  - comparisons: `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`
  - arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `\`, `**`
  - everything inside `{ }` aggregate or choice braces

Variables on the right of `:` inside an aggregate are LOCAL to that aggregate.
You must bind them outside as well if you reference them outside.

End your program with `#show output/3.` so only output cells appear in the answer set.

</clingo_essentials>

<example>
This puzzle copies all non-zero cells from input to output and leaves zero cells unchanged.

<example_grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</example_grid_1>

<example_grid_2>
Input:
<diagram>
0 0 0
0 0 5
0 0 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 0 0
0 0 5
0 0 0
</diagram>
</example_grid_2>

<explanation>
The output is identical to the input: every cell keeps its original color.
</explanation>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example>

% -------------------------------------------------
% 1. grid dimensions
% -------------------------------------------------
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 2. output cell predicate (the whole grid is the output grid)
% -------------------------------------------------
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 3. exactly one colour per output cell
% -------------------------------------------------
1 { output(R,C,Colour) : Colour } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 4. border of the whole grid
% -------------------------------------------------
border(R,C) :- R = 0   ; col(C).          % top row
border(R,C) :- C = 0   ; row(R).          % left column
border(R,C) :- R = n_rows(N)-1 ; col(C). % bottom row
border(R,C) :- C = n_cols(M)-1 ; row(R). % right column

% -------------------------------------------------
% 5. cells that are reachable from the border
%    – start from border cells that are 0
%    – move only to orthogonal neighbours that are also 0
% -------------------------------------------------
reachable(R,C)  :- input(R,C,0),   border(R,C).
reachable(R,C)  :- reachable(R2,C2), adj(R2,C2,R,C), input(R,C,0).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 5a. 4‑direction adjacency (no arithmetic constraints)
% -------------------------------------------------
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- R = R2+1, C = C2.            % down  (R = R2+1)
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- R2 = R+1, C = C2.            % up   (R2 = R+1)
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- C = C2+1, R = R2.            % right
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- C2 = C+1, R = R2.            % left

% -------------------------------------------------
% 5b. interior zero: a 0‑cell that is NOT reachable
%      but has at least one orthogonal neighbour that is a 2.
% -------------------------------------------------
interior_zero(R,C) :-
    not reachable(R,C),
    input(R,C,0),
    adj(R2,C2,R,C),
    input(R2,C2,2).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 6. a 2‑cell is interior if it is NOT reachable
%     and it has **no** reachable zero neighbour.
%    (the constraint below will forbid colour 3 for such a cell)
% -------------------------------------------------
has_reachable_zero(R,C) :- adj(R,N,R,C), reachable(N).   % a 2 has a reachable zero neighbour
interior_two(R,C)  :- input(R,C,2), not reachable(R,C).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 7. colour choice
% -------------------------------------------------
% cells that are interior become colour 3, all others become colour 0
1 { output(R,C,0)  : 1 } 1 :- output_cell(R,C), not interior(R,C).
1 { output(R,C,3)  : 1 } 1 :- interior(R,C).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 8. interior definition
% -------------------------------------------------
interior(R,C) :- interior_zero(R,C).
interior(R,C) :- interior_two(R,C).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 9. forbid colour 3 for a 2‑cell that has a reachable zero neighbour
% -------------------------------------------------
:- interior_two(R,C), has_reachable_zero(R,C), output(R,C,3).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 10. show the output grid
#show output/3.
</asp>

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Border zero cells
border_zero(R,C) :- input(R,C,0), R = 0.
border_zero(R,C) :- input(R,C,0), C = 0.
border_zero(R,C) :- input(R,C,0), R = N-1.
border_zero(R,C) :- input(R,C,0), C = M-1.

% Reachable zero cells (connected to border via zero adjacency)
reachable_zero(R,C) :- border_zero(R,C).
reachable_zero(R,C) :- input(R,C,0), adj(R2,C2,R,C), reachable_zero(R2,C2).

% Orthogonal neighbours
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- R2 = R-1, C2 = C.
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- R2 = R+1, C2 = C.
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- C2 = C-1, R2 = R.
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- C2 = C+1, R2 = R.

% Interior zero cells
interior_zero(R,C) :- input(R,C,0), not reachable_zero(R,C).

% Output colours
1 { output(R,C,3) : 1 } 1 :- row(R), col(C), interior_zero(R,C).
1 { output(R,C,0) : 1 } 1 :- row(R), col(C), not interior_zero(R,C).

#show output/3.

  rule:        head :- body.
  constraint:  :- body.

Aggregates go on the right side of `=`:

Choice rules guess values within bounds. Each choice contains exactly ONE atom:
  1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

Modulo is `\`, integer division is `/`. There is no `#mod`, no `//`, no `?:` ternary.

appear in at least one positive (non-negated) predicate. The following do
NOT bind variables:

Variables on the right of `:` inside an aggregate are LOCAL to that aggregate.
You must bind them outside as well if you reference them outside.

% -------------------------------------------------

% -------------------------------------------------
border(R,C) :- R = 0   ; col(C).          % top row

border(R,C) :- R = n_rows(N)-1 ; col(C). % bottom row
border(R,C) :- C = n_cols(M)-1 ; row(R). % right column

% -------------------------------------------------
% 5. cells that are reachable from the border
%    – start from border cells that are 0
%    – move only to orthogonal neighbours that are also 0
% -------------------------------------------------
reachable(R,C)  :- input(R,C,0),   border(R,C).
reachable(R,C)  :- reachable(R2,C2), adj(R2,C2,R,C), input(R,C,0).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 5a. 4‑direction adjacency (no arithmetic constraints)
% -------------------------------------------------
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- R = R2+1, C = C2.            % down  (R = R2+1)
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- R2 = R+1, C = C2.            % up   (R2 = R+1)
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- C = C2+1, R = R2.            % right
adj(R2,C2,R,C) :- C2 = C+1, R = R2.            % left

%      but has at least one orthogonal neighbour that is a 2.

    input(R,C,0),
    adj(R2,C2,R,C),
